1. Suppose that China’s central bank, the PBOC, has decided to appreciate the value of the Chinese RMB by
intervening in the foreign exchange market. Explain the effect of this ‘strong currency policy’ on the
following:
a. The price and number of wool sweaters imported from Pakistan into China.
______________________________________________________________________________________
b. The demand from Chinese people for the Pakistani currency of Rupees.
______________________________________________________________________________________
c. The price (in Pakistan) and amount of Chinese goods exported to Pakistan.
______________________________________________________________________________________
d. The demand from Pakistani people for Chinese RMB.
______________________________________________________________________________________
e. The Chinese balance of trade (NX).
______________________________________________________________________________________
f. The PBOC’s foreign exchange reserves, if it maintains this ‘strong currency policy’ for some time.
______________________________________________________________________________________

2. Suppose that the ECB, the European Central Bank, is loosening monetary policy and lowering interest
rates. Explain the effects of this policy change on each of the following:
a. The US dollar exchange rate vs the Euro
______________________________________________________________________________________
b. United States balance of trade with Europe (NX)
______________________________________________________________________________________

3. Explain whether each of these people would prefer a strong or a weak currency, and why.
a. A rice farmer in rural China, who has to compete with imported rice from South East Asia.
______________________________________________________________________________________
b. The owner of a furniture company that produces mainly for the export market.
______________________________________________________________________________________
c. A production manager at a bicycle factory that imports parts and produces bicycles for the domestic
market. Assume that Chinese consumers do not buy foreign made bicycles.
______________________________________________________________________________________
d. A Chinese consumer.
______________________________________________________________________________________

4. This question examines why it should be the case that, in equilibrium, differences in inflation & nominal
interest rates are reflected by appreciation or depreciation of the exchange rate. Note that the calculations
below assume that interest rates, inflation and exchange rates are in equilibrium. As such, the results hold
true only in the Long Run.

Your Aunt Emily from England has given you ₤10,000 to help pay for your son’s college tuition in Hong
Kong. Your son is 12 years old, and you won’t need the money for several years. You are trying to decide
between keeping the money in Hong Kong dollars (HKD) or British pounds (GBP). Suppose that inflation
rate in Hong Kong is 3% per year, and inflation in Britain is 1% per year. And, nominal interest rates in HK
are 5% per year.
Assume that it currently takes HK$ 10.00 to buy ₤ 1.00

i)   If real interest rates are similar in HK and Britain, what are nominal interest rates in Britain?
______________________________________________________________________________________
______________________________________________________________________________________

ii)  If you left the ₤10,000 in a bank in England, how much money will you have at the end of the year?
______________________________________________________________________________________
______________________________________________________________________________________

iii) If you converted the money and left $100,000 in a bank in HK, how much money will you have at the
   end of the year?
______________________________________________________________________________________
______________________________________________________________________________________

iv) If nominal exchange rates do not change over the year, which currency should you keep the money in?
  How much more would you earn?
______________________________________________________________________________________
______________________________________________________________________________________

v)  If the exchange rate changes according to purchasing power parity, by how many percent would the HK
    dollar appreciate or depreciate against the British pounds? What will the HK dollars - British pounds
   exchange rate be in one year’s time?
______________________________________________________________________________________
______________________________________________________________________________________
______________________________________________________________________________________

vi) Suppose that exchange rates change as you predict in (v).  If you convert ₤10,000 into Hong Kong
    dollars, deposit it into a Hong Kong bank and convert it back into British pounds at the end of the year.
  How much would you have? How much profit or loss would you make, compared with if you left the
   money in a bank in England?
   (Assume that you can costlessly convert your money between HK$ and British pounds.)
______________________________________________________________________________________
